description: This bar chart illustrates the variance explained by two methods, MVS and 1-MVS, across different LLMs and data sizes. The horizontal axis represents the LLM and data size combinations, with categories labeled “70B llama”, “65 llama”, “70B llama”, “65 llama”, “70B llama”, and “65 llama”, appearing in this order. The vertical axis, labeled “Variance Explained”, ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with a linear scale and tick marks at 0.2 intervals. Each category has two stacked bars; the lower portion of each bar is teal and represents MVS, while the upper portion is purple and represents 1-MVS. For “70B llama”, the MVS bar reaches approximately 0.58, and the 1-MVS bar extends to approximately 0.96, resulting in a total bar height of 1.0. For “65 llama”, the MVS bar reaches approximately 0.22, and the 1-MVS bar extends to approximately 0.78, also resulting in a total bar height of 1.0. The bars are arranged in pairs, alternating between “70B llama” and “65 llama”. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
